rounds.proof_sketch: For T=float (torch.float32 inputs): static_cast<float>(float_val) is identity, and 'return float_val' where return type is float is also identity. For T=double: both explicit static_cast<float>(double_val) and implicit conversion (return double_val as float) perform identical IEEE-754 narrowing conversion. For T=__half: unchanged specialization handles this case. No value can distinguish the expressions.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes an explicit static_cast<float>(val) from the generic to_float<T> template, leaving just 'return val'. Since the return type is float, C++ performs an implicit conversion that is semantically identical to the explicit cast. For T=float (the input dtype), both expressions are no-ops. For T=double, both explicit and implicit conversions follow the same IEEE-754 rounding rules. For T=__half, a separate template specialization (which was NOT mutated) handles the conversion via __half2float(). The mutation is semantically equivalent for all supported types and all possible input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: UNKILLABLE - The mutation is semantically equivalent. In C++, returning a value with implicit conversion to the return type produces identical results to an explicit static_cast for standard numeric types. No input value within the fixed shape contract can distinguish between static_cast<float>(val) and the implicit conversion that occurs when returning val from a function with return type float.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should recognize that removing static_cast between identical types (float->float) or where implicit conversion is equivalent (double->float, int->float) produces semantic equivalents. Consider adding a 'semantic_cast_equivalence' rule to Layer 1 static analysis to automatically mark such mutations as equivalent.
